Rest the bar on your upper back (not on your neck), hands a little wider than shoulder width.
Feet about shoulder width apart, toes pointing slightly outwards.
Brace your core, then push your hips back and down while bending your knees.
Go as deep as you can with a straight back – aim: thighs at least parallel to the floor.
Push up powerfully through your whole foot until you're standing upright again.
At the top, breathe in deeply and hold your breath (tight core), push back up from the bottom, breathe out at the top.

Squats without weight or holding a dumbbell in front of your chest (goblet squat).
Lie on the bench with your eyes roughly under the bar, feet firmly on the floor.
Pull your shoulder blades together and down; a slight arch is fine, your bum stays on the bench.
Grip the bar a little wider than shoulder width and lift it off the rack.
Lower it under control to your lower chest, elbows about 45–70° from your body.
Press the bar up powerfully until your arms are almost straight.
Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you press.
Bar bounces off the chest
Elbows flared out at 90°

With heavy weights, always train with a spotter or safety bars.
Keep your wrists straight, the bar sits over your forearms.
Dumbbell bench press or push-ups.
Set the bench to about 30–45° and lie down, feet firmly on the floor.
Pull your shoulder blades together and down.
Hold the weight above your shoulders.
Lower slowly to your upper chest (below the collarbone).
Press straight up.
Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you press.
Bench too steep – then mainly the shoulders work
Shoulders roll forward
Weight only lowered halfway
With dumbbells the movement is freer and gentler on the shoulders.
Incline bench press with light dumbbells.
Lie on a flat bench, dumbbells above your chest, palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows slightly and keep that angle the whole time.
Open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Bring them back together above your chest in the same arc – like a hug.
Breathe in as you open, breathe out as you bring them together.
Arms locked straight – strains the elbows
Lowering too far
It turns into a press with heavily bent arms
Better lighter and clean: flys are an isolation exercise, not a strength exercise.
Flys on the cable machine or the pec deck.
Place your hands a little wider than shoulder width under your shoulders.
Bring your body into a straight line from head to toe, core and glutes tight.
Lower your chest towards the floor under control, elbows pointing diagonally back.
Just before the floor, push back up until your arms are almost straight.
Hips sag
Bum sticks up
Head drops
Better fewer reps and all the way down.
Push-ups on a bench or on your knees.
Support yourself on the parallel bars, arms straight, shoulders away from your ears.
Bend your legs slightly and lean your upper body a little forward.
Bend your elbows backwards and lower until your upper arms are about horizontal.
Push back up until your arms are straight.
Lowering too far – strains the shoulders
Shoulders shrug up to the ears
Momentum from the legs
More forward lean = more chest, more upright = more triceps.
If your shoulders hurt, reduce the depth.
Bench dips (hands behind you on a bench) or assisted dips on the machine.
Sit upright on a bench with a backrest, feet firmly on the floor.
Hold the bar a little wider than shoulder width in front of your upper chest, elbows under your hands.
Tighten your core and glutes.
Press the bar straight overhead, moving your head briefly back.
Lower under control back to chin height.
Breathe in before pressing, breathe out as you press.
Strong arch in the lower back
Bar is pressed forward instead of straight up
Half movement
At the top, hands, elbows and shoulders are stacked.
Shoulder press with dumbbells or on the machine.
Stand upright, dumbbells at your sides, elbows slightly bent.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they're about horizontal.
Hold briefly at the top; the elbows lead the movement.
Lower slowly again.
Breathe out as you lift, breathe in as you lower.
Momentum from the upper body
Shoulders shrug up to the ears
Arms higher than shoulder height
A light weight is enough – the side shoulder is a small muscle.
Lowering slowly makes a big difference.
Single-arm lateral raises on the cable machine or with very light dumbbells.
Stand upright, dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Raise your arms forward with slightly bent elbows.
Lift to about shoulder height.
Leaning back with the upper body
Using momentum
Lifting too high
Brace your core so your back stays still.
Alternating left and right works too.
Front raises with a weight plate or light dumbbells.
Set the rope attachment on the cable machine to head height.
Grip the rope with both hands and step back, arms straight.
Pull the rope towards your face, elbows go up and out.
At the end, pull your hands apart next to your ears and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Return under control.
Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you return.
Leaning back with the whole body
Elbows drop down
Weight too heavy
Good for posture and healthy shoulders – rather many reps.
With a resistance band on a door or bar.
Grip the bar a little wider than shoulder width (palms facing forward).
Hang with arms almost straight, actively pull your shoulders down.
Pull your chest towards the bar until your chin is over the bar.
Lower under control back to an almost straight hang.
Breathe out as you pull up, breathe in as you lower.
Swinging the legs (kipping)
Only half reps
Shoulders hang loose up by the ears
Can't do a pull-up? Train just the slow lowering (negative pull-ups).
Pull-ups with a resistance band, assisted on the machine, or lat pulldown.
Sit down and wedge your thighs under the pads.
Grip the bar a little wider than shoulder width.
Lean your upper body slightly back, chest out.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, elbows down and back.
Slowly guide it back up until your arms are straight.
Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you return.

Swinging far back
Letting the weight drop at the top

Bend your knees slightly and lean your upper body forward with a straight back (about 30–45°).
Pull the bar to your lower belly, elbows close to your body.
At the top, squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower under control until your arms are straight.
Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower.

Dumbbell row supported on the bench.
Support one knee and the same hand on a bench, the other leg stands on the floor.
Back straight, roughly parallel to the floor.
Let the dumbbell hang with your arm straight.
Pull the dumbbell towards your hip, elbow close to your body.
Lower slowly again. Then switch sides.
Upper body twists open
Pulling to the chest instead of the hip

Push your hips back, bend your knees and grip the bar shoulder-width.
Back straight, chest out, shoulders slightly in front of the bar, core tight.
Push the floor away with your legs, pulling the bar up close to your body.
Stand upright at the top (don't lean back), then lower under control with a straight back.
Breathe in at the bottom and hold your breath, breathe out at the top.

Romanian deadlift with dumbbells or kettlebell deadlift.
Set up the back extension bench (Roman chair): pad under your hip bones, feet secure.
Cross your arms in front of your chest.
Bend forward and down with a straight back.
Come back up until your upper body and legs form a line.
Don't overextend into an arched back.
Breathe out as you come up, breathe in as you lower.
